transcript.text: Hi, I'm Sensei. Put your page under the camera and start solving. I'm watching.
Okay I did it. x squared plus 9 is 25, so x is 4 or minus 4. Easy.
You're close, but there's a mistake in the first step. When you expand (x + 3)^2, you need to multiply the whole thing by itself, not just square the terms.
No, the power distributes. Like 2x squared is 4x squared. Same thing here, x squared plus 9.
The power doesn't distribute like that. When you square a sum, you multiply the whole thing by itself. Try (x + 3)(x + 3) and see what you get.
Why not? It works for 2x squared. Why is a plus any different?
The power doesn't distribute over addition. When you square a sum, you multiply it by itself. Try (x + 3)(x + 3) and see what you get.
Fine. x times x, x times 3, 3 times x, 3 times 3. Wait, thats x squared plus 6x plus 9?

Okay so x squared plus 6x plus 9 is 25, minus 25, x plus 8 times x minus 2, so x is 2 or minus 8?
You're on the right track with expanding the square. Now, to solve the equation, subtract 25 from both sides and simplify. What do you get when you do that?
